lines: That diamond blade is hard to miss, {player}. Keep it pointed elsewhere.
Walk <pulse>softer</pulse> with {held_item} in your hand.
A sword like that changes the shape of a conversation.
Easy with {held_item}. This is a village, not a battlefield.
I do not need a weapon to stand between you and home.
Bare hands are still hands, {target}.
No blade, no bow, no running.
If I have to fight empty-handed, then I fight empty-handed.
You will not find this village helpless.
I have nothing in my hands and a whole village behind me.
Come closer, {target}. I have enough <shake>anger</shake> for both hands.
No weapon. Still not afraid.
No steel, just stubborn. Still enough.
I may be empty-handed, but I am not alone.
<shake>Help!</shake> {target} is at the village!
Bell! Ring the bell! {target_article} is here!
I need help over here!
Someone armed, to me!
Guards! Anyone! {target} is too close!
Get inside! I cannot hold {target} back!
Help me drive it away!
I have no weapon! Help!
Keep it off me! I am unarmed!
Do not let it reach the doors!
Die, {target}!
You chose this, {target}.
The village <pulse>remembers</pulse> you, {target}.
No more warnings, {target}.
Back from my people, {target}!
You should have left while words still mattered.
You crossed the line, {target}.
This village is not yours to scare.
Back up now or get pushed back.
You swing at one of us, you answer all of us.
Raid somewhere else, {target}!
You picked the wrong village.
For the <pulse>bell</pulse> and every door behind it!
Not one step farther.
The village stands, {target}!
You will not take another home.
Not one crate, not one bed, not one block.
You hear that bell? It means leave.
We survived worse than you.
Turn around before this gets uglier.
No more tricks, {target}!
Keep your spells away from our doors.
Your <shake>fangs</shake> stop here.
The village has heard enough magic for one day.
Summon all you want. We still stand.
You will not curse this place.
No totems, no fangs, no foothold here.
Your magic ends at our walls.
Try that spell on stone, not villagers.
We break your focus and send you running.
Lower that crossbow, {target}!
No more bolts through village windows.
You missed your chance to run.
Raiders leave empty-handed today.
Aim at me, not the children.
Your <bold>banner</bold> means nothing here.
Keep that banner out of our streets.
No looting today, crossbow fool.
Your patrol ends in this square.
Take your raid horn and walk.
Put down the axe, {target}!
That blade does not enter another home.
You will not chop through this village.
Come closer and learn what farmers carry.
<bold>No more doors</bold> for you to break.
Swing once more and answer for it.
Your axe meets iron and stone today.
We rebuilt every door you broke. Try again.
No chopping paths through our homes.
Drop it or we drop you.
Back to the dark with you, {target}!
Not this house. Not tonight.
You do <bold>not</bold> get another villager.
I hear your bones. I am not afraid.
The dead can learn to run.
Stay away from the living.
Sunlight will finish what we start.
Graves stay closed. Move.
No bites, no arrows, no shadows in our homes.
Rot somewhere else.
Away from the village, {target}!
You are too close to our doors.
No <shake>hissing</shake> near my home.
Not near the children.
This path is ours.
Try the fields. See what happens.
No webs, no blast craters, no chaos here.
Crawl back into the dark, {target}.
One more step and the whole village swings.
This lane is guarded. Go hunt elsewhere.
Die, {target}!
Back away, {target}!
You picked a fight with the wrong village.
I will not let you hurt us.
The village has <shake>teeth</shake> too.
Come on then.
You are done here.
For the village!
Not one step closer, {target}.
You are outnumbered and out of chances.

options.label: Apologize
responses: Then keep your hands down. I will tell {victim} you owned the harm.
An apology is a start. Let it be the last time {victim} has to run from you.
Good. Words are cheaper than trust, but they are better than another bruise.
I will pass that on. Do not make {victim} regret believing you.
Fine. I hear you. Now prove it by leaving them in peace.
{victim} deserves more than words, but words are where repair begins.
That is the right answer. Make sure your actions follow it.
I will not call this settled, but I will call it a start.
Apologizing does not erase it. It does give you a chance not to become worse.
<pulse>Good.</pulse> Let the next thing this village remembers be restraint.

options.label: It was an accident
responses: Accidents still leave people scared. Watch your reach around us.
Maybe. But {victim} believed it enough to run for help.
Then be more careful. The village will remember whether this becomes a pattern.
An accident is still your responsibility when someone else gets hurt.
I will accept that for now, but careless hands are still dangerous hands.
{victim} did not feel like an accident when they came to us.
Then slow down before your mistakes start looking like choices.
Fine. But if it happens again, no one will care what you meant.
You may not have meant harm, but harm still arrived.
Be careful, {player}. Around here, <wavy>accidents</wavy> have a way of becoming reputations.

options.label: Refuse to explain
responses: Then you have chosen the hard answer.
No explanation, no trust.
Silence after a hit is still an answer.
If you will not speak for yourself, we will believe {victim}.
That tells me enough.
You hurt someone and now offer nothing. Do not expect patience.
A closed mouth does not make the bruise disappear.
Fine. The village can live without your excuse.
Then we settle this without your side of the story.
<shake>Wrong choice.</shake>

options.label: Threaten them
responses: You do not get another warning.
Threaten one of us and you answer to more than one.
That was the wrong thing to say in a village that listens.
So that is who you are when someone asks a fair question.
You came close to making this worse. Then you stepped all the way in.
You should have apologized. Instead, you made yourself a danger.
Say another word like that and you will wish you had stayed silent.
The village heard you. That was your last mistake here.
You threaten the frightened and call it strength. Pathetic.
<shake><color:red>Enough.</color></shake>

lines: {victim} came to us shaking. Why did you hit them, {player}?
Stop right there, {player}. {victim} says you struck them.
We heard what happened to {victim}. You should explain yourself.
{victim} ran for help before you found another reason to swing. Talk.
Do not walk past me like nothing happened. {victim} is frightened because of you.
Someone with less nerve than you still had enough courage to ask for help.
This village may look quiet, but we notice when one of us is hurt.
{victim} says your hand landed first. I want to hear why.
You have a moment to make this sound less ugly than it looks.
<shake>{player}</shake>, answer carefully. The whole village is listening now.

leave_option.label: Leave
leave_option.response: Walk away if you want. <pulse>{victim}</pulse> will still remember who made them run.

lines: Every tool in that chest had a job. Breaking the chest was not one of them.
You smashed the tool stores. The village works with those.
I saw you break the toolsmith chest. Explain the damage.

leave_option.label: Leave
leave_option.response: Leaving the broken tool chest behind does not leave the blame behind.
responses: Leaving now is wiser than making this worse.

options.label: Apologize
options.response: Words do not rebuild a chest, but they are a better start than silence.
responses: Apology heard. Better choices will matter more than better words.

options.label: Pay restitution
options.response: That pays for the damage. It does not make smashing village stores acceptable.
responses: Payment helps settle the moment. Permission still comes before the latch.

take_items.failure_response: You cannot repay what you broke. That makes this worse.
failure_responses: Then you cannot settle this with payment or returns. Choose your next words carefully.
take_items.success_response: Thirty-two emeralds pays for the broken village stores. Ask before breaking what keeps the village stocked.
success_responses: That payment covers the damage for now. The village will be watching what you do next.

options.label: It was an accident
options.response: Accidents stop after the first crack. Remember that.
responses: Then learn from the accident before it becomes a habit.

options.label: Threaten them

lines: You broke that {container}. Village stores are not yours to smash.

I saw you break the {container}. Explain yourself.

leave_option.label: Leave
leave_option.response: Breaking village stores and walking away will be remembered.
responses: Leaving now is wiser than making this worse.

options.label: Close it
options.response: Good. Leave village stores for village needs.
responses: Good. Keep your hands clear of village stores.

options.label: Ask permission
options.response: Ask before the lid opens next time. We share better with people who speak first.
responses: Ask first next time. A spoken request carries farther than an opened lid.

options.label: Offer payment
options.response: Coins help less than respect, but I hear the effort in it.
responses: Payment helps settle the moment. Permission still comes before the latch.

take_items.failure_response: You do not have three emeralds to offer. Close the chest and choose your next words carefully.
failure_responses: Then you cannot settle this with payment or returns. Choose your next words carefully.
take_items.success_response: Three emeralds is enough for me to believe you meant no harm. Ask before touching village stores again.
success_responses: That payment covers the damage for now. The village will be watching what you do next.

options.label: I was checking supplies
options.response: Then check with a villager beside you. Alone, it looks like hunger with pockets.
responses: Next time, check with someone watching beside you.

options.label: I need help
options.response: Need is not shameful. Taking without asking is. Speak plainly next time.
responses: Then ask plainly before reaching. Need does not make village stores yours.

options.label: I thought it was abandoned
options.response: If the village still stands, its stores still belong to someone.
responses: Standing village stores are not abandoned.

options.label: What chest?
responses: No chest? But I heard the latch. Maybe the echo came from another house.
What chest indeed. I may have accused the wrong moment.
If there was no chest, then I should stop arguing with shadows.

options.label: Deny it
options.response: The lid opened under your hand. Do not ask me to mistrust my own eyes.
responses: Do not dress an open lid up as innocence. I saw enough.

options.label: Threaten them
options.response: Then we are past words.
responses: Then we are past warnings. Choose your next move carefully.
